why: Go matters for DevOps because many of the core tools, including Docker, Kubernetes, and Terraform, are written in Go.

basics.title: Install Go, go mod init, go run, go build
basics.note: go mod init example.com/hello creates a go.mod file for your module. go run . compiles and runs the program; go build creates a binary you can ship.
basics.readme: Install Go, `go mod init`, `go run`, `go build`

basics.title: Variables, types, if / for / switch
basics.note: x := 5 declares a variable and infers its type; var x int = 5 is the longer form. for is Go's only loop keyword. switch cases do not fall through unless you write fallthrough.

basics.title: Slices and maps
basics.note: A slice is a flexible view over an array; grow it with append. A map is a hash table: v, ok := m[key] tells you whether the key exists.

basics.title: Structs and methods
basics.note: A struct groups fields. A method is a function with a receiver, like func (u User) Name() string. Use a pointer receiver (*User) when the method needs to change the struct.

basics.title: Interfaces
basics.note: An interface is a list of methods. Any type that has those methods satisfies the interface automatically; there is no implements keyword.

basics.title: Error handling (if err != nil)
basics.note: Functions return an error as their last value. Check it right away with if err != nil, and add context with fmt.Errorf("reading config: %w", err).

basics.title: Goroutines and channels
basics.note: go f() runs f concurrently in a goroutine. Channels (make(chan int)) pass values between goroutines safely; sync.WaitGroup waits for a group of goroutines to finish.

basics.title: Testing with go test and table-driven tests
basics.note: Tests live in files ending in _test.go as func TestXxx(t *testing.T). A table-driven test loops over a slice of {input, want} cases, often using t.Run for each case.
basics.readme: Testing with `go test` and table-driven tests

resolve.title: Two Sum
resolve.note: Practice maps: map[int]int from value to index.

resolve.title: Valid Parentheses
resolve.note: Use a slice as a stack: append to push, s[:len(s)-1] to pop.

resolve.title: Reverse Linked List
resolve.note: Practice structs and pointers with a *ListNode type.

resolve.title: Binary Search
resolve.note: Practice index math; lo + (hi-lo)/2 avoids overflow in languages with fixed-size integers.

tools.title: CLI that counts lines and words in a file (flag, os)
tools.note: Read the file path from a flag, open it with os.Open, and count with a bufio.Scanner.
tools.readme: CLI that reads a file and counts lines and words (uses `flag` and `os`)

tools.title: HTTP health checker for a list of URLs (status codes and response times)
tools.note: Use an http.Client with a Timeout. For each URL, record resp.StatusCode and time.Since(start).
tools.readme: HTTP health checker: send requests to a list of URLs and report status codes and response times

tools.title: Concurrent version with goroutines
tools.note: Check each URL in its own goroutine and collect results through a channel, or wait with a sync.WaitGroup.
tools.readme: Concurrent version of the health checker using goroutines

tools.title: Tiny REST API with net/http that returns JSON, plus tests
tools.note: Write JSON with encoding/json in your handlers, and test them with net/http/httptest without starting a real server.
tools.readme: Tiny REST API with `net/http` that returns JSON, plus tests
